answer: Cross-epoch behaviour matching. Each identity's action vector, rate limits and counterparty mix are hashed per epoch; a new epoch only inherits standing if its trajectory stays within a bounded divergence of the prior one. Fleets bought for a single voyage cannot pivot cheaply, since abrupt pattern shifts force re-establishment from zero reputation. An attacker must sustain many identities through consistent behaviour across epochs, paying continuous compute and coordination cost, with no safe haven for dormant sockpuppets, while organic growth accretes like timber.
